A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DiffInk work and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–E. Matching equations, Tables 1–5, and Figures 1–18 support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original handwriting-generation comparisons, ablations, sampling-step experiments, English handwriting examples, and OCR experiments using synthesized data.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the quantitative evaluations in Tables 1–5 and qualitative experiments in Appendices C–D.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and Appendix B retain the same InkVAE regularization losses, ConvNeXt-V2 content encoder, InkDiT architecture, and diffusion training and sampling procedures. No method component is added or revised.

E1.justification: Both use CASIA-OLHWDB text lines and isolated-character augmentation, IAM-OnDB English handwriting, and ICDAR13 OCR evaluation. The style-mixing, one-shot, layout, and paragraph-generation scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Drawing, DeepImitator, WLU, SDT, and OLHWG. Table 5 retains the CNN+Transformer and GLRNet comparisons with real-only versus augmented training data. Citation replacements do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The writer splits, preprocessing, training budgets, reference-segment comparison protocol, evaluation metrics, and sampling settings match throughout Section 4 and Appendices A–D. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: The loss and architecture ablations, DDIM-step sensitivity study, t-SNE visualizations, layout-error analyses, and style-control case studies are retained. Figure 4 redisplays existing examples without adding an analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without explicit repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–5 are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports DiffInk AR 94.38%, CR 94.58%, Style 77.38, DTW 1.049, and 58.47 characters/second in both. The qualitative samples and findings are also retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives, and diffusion expressions in Section 3 and Appendix B, including Equations 1–9, are unchanged. Neither version introduces additional propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty, full-line generation, latent regularization, fidelity, and efficiency claims. Replacing 'state-of-the-art' with 'SOTA' does not alter their meaning or scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning structured latent representations, coupled character and layout modeling, and the sampling quality–speed tradeoff remain unchanged. Appendix D retains the same applicability discussion and limitation that other languages require retraining.

D1.justification: Architecture specifications, preprocessing instructions, hyperparameters, hardware, training times, and the stated code link are retained. The shortened reproducibility statement summarizes existing sections without changing the available technical information.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 replaces Jiang et al.'s speech-synthesis citation with Lee et al.'s HierSpeech++. The OpenAI reference changes from the ChatGPT webpage to the GPT-4 technical report. Other bibliography updates largely concern existing works' metadata; research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v4 introduces consistent SOTA abbreviation, adds Huiguo He as a corresponding author and a funding acknowledgement, shortens the reproducibility statement, and makes punctuation and bibliography edits. The scientific exposition and section organization remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 4 has clearer handwriting rendering and corrects the swapped horizontal and rising-layout column headings while retaining the samples. Figure 8 and page 10 spacing are adjusted, and the title is rewrapped. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: Correcting Figure 4's swapped layout headings and improving its rendering makes the central qualitative comparison more accurate and readable. The cleaner title and shorter reproducibility summary provide additional editorial polish. Methods, empirical support, technical disclosures, and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
